      "description": "Run the detector to get ratios you can compare with this chart.",
      "url": "https://myfaceshapechart.com/face-shape-chart",
      "source_url": "https://myfaceshapechart.com/face-shape-chart",
      "content_markdown": "# Face Shape Chart: How to Read Your Result

Use a face shape chart in this order: record four measurements, find the largest line, compare face length with face width, and use the jawline as the tie-breaker. The four readings are forehead width, cheekbone width, jawline width, and face length. A chart becomes useful when it explains the close calls between rows instead of pretending every face fits one perfect box.

## 1. Prepare the Photo or Mirror View

Pull all hair away from the forehead and jaw. Use a straight-on mirror view or a front-facing photo, with no fringe covering the outline. Keep the head level while you inspect the chart. These are the first three operations because hair, tilt, and a three-quarter angle can change which part looks widest.

Do not begin with a celebrity comparison. Begin with the visible outline and the same view you will use for every row.

## 2. Record Four Lines

Use a flexible tape and a notebook or phone. The chart uses four lines:

1. **Forehead width:** measure across the widest part, usually between the eyebrow area and the hairline.
2. **Cheekbone width:** measure from the outer point of one cheekbone to the other.
3. **Jawline width:** measure from the center of the chin to the point where one jaw angles upward toward the ear, then multiply that one-side reading by 2.
4. **Face length:** measure from the center of the hairline to the tip of the chin.

The multiplication in step 3 matters. A one-side jaw reading cannot be compared directly with a full forehead or cheekbone reading. Write the four results in one order every time: forehead, cheekbones, jaw, length.
